analysis: The only changed file is a Swift test file, ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift. The change is the new test at head lines 191-230, theDaemonStateReportsTheFilterACommittedSwitchApplied. It covers an accepted and a refused model-replacement commit, and checks that state.json reports enabled_models_at_start and enabled_models_at_last_switch. It also checks that the saved provider.toml holds the new enabled_models after acceptance and the old ones after rollback. The test uses MockCoordinator, a temporary directory and a local snapshot. It introduces no production code, no endpoint, no key handling and no authorization change. Nothing in it touches the threat-model assets: the X25519 or SE keys, the App Attest authorization, the prefix cache of T-041, or the fan helper. The temp directories hold no secrets, and cleanup runs through defer. The test exercises existing production behavior around the model-switch drain barrier, the coordinator validate-then-commit-then-rollback flow, and the daemon state file. That behavior is the model-selection fail-closed path in TB-002 and TB-007. The test supports the rollback guarantee, so it adds no regression. Production files such as ProviderLoop that write enabled_models_at_last_switch are not supplied in this batch. Their correctness and the state-file permissions cannot be judged from this evidence. That is an integration question for the production changes, not a finding here. The patch excerpt was truncated, but the full head text of the test was visible and reviewed.
